text: A 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes for 10 years presents for follow-up of poorly controlled glucose. Her HbA1c is 9.1%. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and has for two years. She has hypertension treated with lisinopril. She has no history of heart failure. Kidney function is normal with an eGFR of 85 mL/min/1.73m2. She is postmenopausal.

A 45-year-old man presents with severe persistent asthma. He uses a high-dose inhaled corticosteroid and a long-acting beta agonist but has had three exacerbations requiring oral steroids in the past year. He is a former smoker with a 5 pack-year history who quit 10 years ago. Blood eosinophils are elevated at 450 cells/uL. Chest CT shows no other lung disease.
